title: Runtime configuration — the only remote-control surface
description: Served verbatim by GET /v1/config from the single row of D1 `runtime_config`. Every value here is changeable with one `wrangler d1 execute` and no app release (FR-033, Constitution X.3). Keep the payload small: it gates app launch.

min_supported_version.description: Force-update gate. The client MUST fail open if this endpoint is unreachable.

update_url.description: Where the app's Update required button sends the learner: the store listing the app is currently distributed through. Optional; absent means the landing site.

killed_problem_ids.description: A problem found wrong in the wild is killed here, same day, no release. The daily falls back to another.

ads.description: The ad kill switch. `enabled: false` takes both ad surfaces — the rewarded hint video and the assessment interstitial — off every install on its next launch, no release, no store review. This is the ONLY thing deciding whether ads run — there is no compile-time switch behind it. Absent means off, as does a relay the app has not reached yet.

enabled.description: false takes both ad surfaces off everywhere.

rotation.description: The global daily pointer. Present means every install — new or long-standing — is handed the SAME problem on a given day: index(start_problem_id) + whole days since anchor_date, wrapped around the id-sorted evergreen pool. Absent means each install walks its own un-attempted problems (the pre-pointer behaviour). Restart everyone at problem one by setting start_problem_id to the first id and anchor_date to today — one D1 write, no release. A problem authored for exactly today still wins over the pointer, and a start_problem_id that is withdrawn or missing degrades to the first problem in the pool rather than stranding the day.

start_problem_id.description: The problem served on anchor_date itself.

anchor_date.description: UTC calendar day the pointer sits on start_problem_id. Days before it clamp to the anchor rather than walking backwards.

turn_cap.description: Enforced server-side from the D1 counter, never from the payload (FR-008). THIS IS THE PRIMARY QUOTA LEVER — see research.md R-007.

wrap_up_at_turn.description: From this turn index onward routes/chat.ts substitutes the {{WRAP_UP}} block into the tutor prompt so the learner is steered toward a close rather than cut off at the cap (FR-008a, O2).

min_turn_chars.description: Below this an EMPTY_TURN is returned before the provider is called, so it costs the learner nothing.

model.description: Not a constant. Free-tier catalogues churn.

provider.description: Default for a learner-keyed request that names no provider. NOT the only provider: the learner picks by picking which key to paste (FR-008b), and `X-Provider` on /v1/chat and /v1/judge selects among `keyed_providers`.

keyed_providers.description: Which providers a learner may bring a key for, in the order key entry should offer them. Served verbatim by GET /v1/config so the app's provider list changes with no release. An `X-Provider` value outside this list is BAD_REQUEST — a provider the operator has not offered is refused, not silently redirected. Absent means the single `provider` value, which is the pre-per-key-routing behaviour.

providers.description: Per-provider overrides for the LEARNER-KEYED path only. A provider with no entry here falls back to the top-level `model` and `trim.condense_model`. CARRIES NO base_url BY DESIGN: the keyed path resolves its host from a table compiled into the Worker, because a remote-controlled base_url here would let one config write redirect every learner's own API key to an arbitrary host. `trial.pool[].base_url` is configurable precisely because those are the operator's own credentials, not a learner's.

repair.description: Transcript repair (feature 004). Absent means repair is off, which is the pre-feature behaviour. THE MODEL NAME HERE IS A FREE-TIER CATALOGUE ENTRY AND WILL CHURN — that is why it is a D1 value and not a constant.

enabled.description: FR-010's kill switch. False means the app never calls and never holds the review step.

min_chars.description: FR-011. Non-whitespace characters. Below this, no round trip. THIS IS THE PRIMARY LEVER IF SC-005's 5% TOKEN BUDGET IS BREACHED.

max_input_chars.description: Bounded input. Sized above a full 90-second recording (~1400 chars).

timeout_ms.description: The Worker's provider timeout AND the app's review-step hold window. One number, two places. Bounded by SC-004's 2 seconds.

min_word_overlap.description: Guard 3. The guard that catches a model answering the problem instead of correcting the transcript.

trial.description: The trial profile. Deliberately NOT the keyed profile: a trial is paid for out of a fixed operator allowance shared by every new install, while a keyed session is paid for by one learner and competes with nobody (FR-031a, research.md R-011).

turn_cap.description: Trial turn cap. Enforced from the SAME D1 turn_counter as keyed turns (FR-032a), against THIS value rather than chat.turn_cap. Six turns is what the demonstration needs — the tutor pushing back and withholding lands in the first three.

ground_truth_tier.description: "A" sends Tier A only, skipping Tier B narrowing (data-model.md §B3). A six-turn session barely reaches trim.narrow_after_turn anyway, so Tier B buys almost nothing and costs ~550 tokens per turn.

condense.description: False at turn_cap <= trim.verbatim_turns, where no turn ever falls out of the verbatim window and a condensation call would be pure waste. Must be revisited if turn_cap is raised above verbatim_turns.

daily_session_cap.description: Optional hard ceiling on trial sessions started per day across all installs, independent of tokens. 0 disables it and lets the token budgets bind. A blunt second guard for the day a link goes wide.

ip_daily_session_cap.description: New trial sessions per network (keyed hash of the caller's IP, never the IP) per UTC day. 0 disables it. Over the cap the relay answers TRIAL_IP_LIMIT and the app offers key entry.

pool.description: Ordered trial provider pool (FR-031b). Capacity is the SUM of several free tiers. TWO RULES, both hard: (1) one account per provider, and only DISTINCT providers — several accounts at one provider is rate-limit evasion, violates provider terms, and is prohibited regardless of the capacity it would buy; (2) every member MUST be a free tier requiring no payment method, so Constitution X.2 holds for the operator as it does for the learner. Selection order and leg eligibility: data-model.md §B8.

id.description: Stable key. Used as the trial_budget primary key and written to usage.provider — so per-member spend is queryable without a schema change.

secret_binding.description: Name of the Worker secret holding this member's credential. The credential itself NEVER appears here, in source, or in a build artifact (FR-025). This field is the NAME of a binding, not a value.

base_url.description: OpenAI-compatible chat-completions base. Members that are not OpenAI-compatible need a provider implementation and must stay enabled:false until it exists.

daily_token_budget.description: Input+output tokens this member may spend per UTC day on the trial path. Set BELOW the provider's published daily allowance, never equal to it — the last call before the ceiling must be one we declined, not one they refused.

structured_output.description: True only if this member genuinely supports strict json_schema decoding. THE JUDGE LEG IS ELIGIBLE ONLY ON TRUE (O3). Do not set true on a claim of 'JSON mode'; that is not the same guarantee, and FR-014's structural impossibility rests on this being strict.

enabled.description: FAILS CLOSED. A member stays false until three things are verified: its free tier requires no payment method, its published RPM/TPD are known, and — for structured_output:true — strict json_schema decoding is confirmed.

cooldown_ms.description: How long a member is skipped after it returns a rate limit. A 429 on the trial path routes to the next member; it never reaches the caller (FR-031c).

verbatim_turns.description: K in data-model.md §B6. Second quota lever after turn_cap.

web.description: The landing site's live demo and notify form (feature 007). Optional: absent means webConfig() falls back to these same defaults. Never sent by GET /v1/config.

enabled.description: Kill switch for the live demo. False falls every visitor back to the scripted demo.

demo_turn_cap.description: Turns a live web demo gets before it ends.

daily_demo_cap.description: Live demos started per UTC day across all visitors.

max_pool_share.description: Share of the trial pool's daily token budget the web demo may spend before it refuses (Constitution X.3).

allowed_origins.description: Exact-match CORS allowlist for the web-only routes (web-cors.ts). Never '*'.
